title: Workload Zeitgeist: continuous batching parameterizer and rollback safety
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: build a continuous batching parameterizer ("Workload Zeitgeist") that profiles live traffic, synthesizes a compact workload signature, and recommends safe batching+cache parameter deltas with automated canary apply and rollback. Unlike previous static profilers, Zeitgeist will maintain a lightweight time-decayed workload model (EWMA of signature features), evaluate candidate parameter sets in shadow/canary mode, and only apply them when cost/latency/eval signals meet configurable safety gates. This ticket covers the engine, heuristics, safety policy, and the operator-facing runbook for gradual apply/rollback.
acceptance_criteria: Zeitgeist produces a deterministic workload signature for a 24h shard with <5% variation when replayed
Engine recommends parameter deltas (microbatch size, kv-window, batching-horizon) with estimated cost delta and impact estimates
End-to-end shadow evaluation pipeline runs on a sample of live traffic and produces cost/latency metrics and QA regression signal within 48h
Automated canary apply will only progress when P95 and P99 latency change <= +10% of baseline AND quality regressions (per prompt-set eval) < 1%
Rollback triggers (latency/cost/quality) execute within 90s and revert config across affected host groups
Documentation and runbook (console rollout UI, metrics dashboard links, manual override) published and reviewed by SRE and Product
tasks: Design signature schema: low-dim feature vector (prompt length distribution, kv-hit-rate, prefix reuse, tail token distribution)
Implement streaming profiler that emits per-minute signatures and compressed daily digest
Build candidate generator: heuristic rules + small evolutionary search for microbatch/kv-window/horizon
Create shadow evaluator: route 1-2% traffic to candidate config in shadow (no apply) and collect cost/latency/quality metrics
Safety policy engine: threshold checks, gradual step sizes, rollback circuit breaker
Integrate canary apply with rollout controller and console hooks for operator visibility
End-to-end tests: synthetic replay harness + smoke on staging with quantifiable asserts
Author runbook and add dashboard panels to console (per-model, per-route cost delta + latency impact)
comments: 2026-03-01 — Aisha Patel: scoped initial requirements after sync with PM (Nora Chen) and SRE. Decision: use EWMA-based time decay for signature stability to avoid oscillation during diurnal shifts.

2026-03-03 — Marcus Li: prototyped signature schema. Sample vectors (24h) compress to ~1.4KB/day per model shard. Early fingerprint can distinguish RLHF chat vs short-completion workloads. Saved prototype in: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Xt-Prot/sample-signature.csv

2026-03-05 — Marcus Li: shadow evaluation harness PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821. Initial results on staging: cost estimate -6.1% with microbatch increase +3, P95 latency +2.3ms (within SLO). Marking as encouraging but need larger sample and quality evals.
2026-03-07 — PM Nora Chen: requested quality regression gating with existing eval harness and adding prompt sets from two enterprise customers (sanitized) to avoid customer impact.

2026-03-09 — Marcus Li: implemented safety policy draft. Canary progression will run in phases: shadow -> 1% canary (10 hosts) -> 10% -> full. Each phase must report pass/fail. Rollback circuit breaker will trip on (a) P99 increase > 15% or (b) evaluation regressions > 1% absolute. Policy doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Workload+Zeitgeist+Safety

2026-03-10 — SRE review (Jamal Ortiz): requested that rollback path include idempotent reconfiguration and a force-revert API that sets a pinned config and emits an incident event. Also requested a throttling mechanism if many hosts fail at once to avoid cascading reboots.

2026-03-11 — Marcus Li: ran a 72h shadow run across three customerlike tenants. Aggregated results uploaded to dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/zeitgeist/summary. Observations: jobs with high prefix reuse benefit most (cost -9%), bursty low-latency workloads show increased tail latency when microbatch steps > 2. Adjusting heuristic to limit step size for high-tail cohorts.

2026-03-12 — Aisha Patel: raised blocker — missing fine-grained telemetry for kv-hit-rate on older runtime nodes (ENG-39107 dependency). We should gate rollout until telemetry is available or fall back to conservative defaults. Added dependency ENG-39107 to the ticket.
2026-03-12 — Marcus Li: created PR for safety policy engine: https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/1293. Needs review from SRE and Security. Tagging Jamal and Priya for review.
